items.title: 68087_Cliff Leeman oral history interview
items.q: Dear friend Milt Hinton... I drop names to you as a friend

ctx.x: interview and recording. As Cliff will tell you on here, after a long session we had the other night, he went home and had some sort of chance to relax, and here he sort of explains himself and recollects. Here are some of his fine recollections -- and Cliff, thank you for this little note telling me what happened.

Dear friend Milt Hinton, this is Sunday, the 25th of February. Yesterday you interviewed me for the first time for my musical and personal history for five solid hours of tapes. It was like breaking the ice in Chesapeake Bay frozen over by the Coast Guard. I'm exhausted today.

We did accomplish so much, and I learned a lot from your interrogations as to the value of explaining names and places -- so they would be understood to those studying the tapes. You see, I drop names to you as a friend, who understands and I expect the uninitiated to understand, also, which they won't without further research on their part.

items.title: 68087_Cliff Leeman oral history interview
items.q: The interviewer (Milton Hinton) introduces himself to Cliff Leeman, and Leeman responds. The interviewee later refers to 'the day with you, Milton'.

ctx.x: Right, right. So we want to get that.

Now I'd like to get this -- you say your name is Cliff Leeman, and most families that I know of, especially black families, of which I am from -- we had more than one -- two names. My name is Milton John Hinton, my grandmother's name was Heddy Liddy Carter Robinson, and I noticed that you only -- and most musicians I have talked to had more than one or two names. Now there is no middle name for you?
Oh, yes; I have a middle name -- Spencer.
